deferred_source_units.source_text: Let him not trust that he will endure, for empty things will result for him.
deferred_source_units.reason: Eliphaz warns the ungodly person not to trust that he will endure, while Psalms 61:10-11 addresses human vanity, injustice, plunder and attachment to wealth. The proposed link depends on supplying wealth as the object of trust in this source sentence; that broad association is not retained as a particular match.

deferred_source_units.source_text: May the branches of his feet be devoured; death will devour his beautiful things.
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual Psalm says that death shepherds people and that their help grows old in Hades away from their glory. It does not say death devours their beauty. A shared personification of death does not establish the proposed devouring-beauty correspondence, and the source is kept pending.
